page: Microsoft Azure D8_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 physical multithreaded cores, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and FMA. Total system memory measures 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage and contains zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent median-level throughput across standard computational workloads. The system achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 4845.0, a stress-ng multi-core result of 7436.34, and a PassMark CPU score of 8381.5. Large-block memory tests show 49.51 GB/sec read and 36.24 GB/sec write bandwidth, facilitating 7.16 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 7.21 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Notable performance dips appear in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 28.22 GB/sec and PassMark physics processing at 832.86, placing these metrics in the lower quartile of tested cloud servers. Similarly, small-model LLM prompt processing delivers 378.97 tokens per second.

Operating with a diskless hardware configuration, the D8_v4 requires external network-attached storage volumes for data persistence. This decoupling isolates persistent state from compute resources while centralizing storage management. Given its balanced resource distribution, the D8_v4 provides an appropriate hardware foundation for enterprise web serving, application middleware, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD build environments, and containerized microservices backed by remote databases.
description: The Microsoft Azure D8_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 physical cores supporting 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on remote managed storage for data persistence. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across enterprise compute tasks, achieving 7.16 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 7.21 GB/sec in static web serving, while exhibiting lower relative throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and physics calculations. Supported by AVX-512 vector instructions and steady memory bandwidth, the D8_v4 is structured for enterprise application tiers, backend APIs, caching layers, and database workloads utilizing remote storage.
